title: Find and interact with network devices
description: Discover IP addresses and services on this Android device’s direct LAN, enroll supported devices, read OpenWrt router DHCP leases and switch Shelly Gen1 relays. Each permission stays under your control.
example: Find a desk lamp on your home network and let your control agent switch its supported relay. Unknown devices stay observations; camera photos keep their separate permission.
options: Find devices and services on this phone's local Wi-Fi or Ethernet network
Enroll supported devices using credentials you authorize
Read OpenWrt router information and DHCP leases; switch Shelly Gen1 relays
Connect supported Tapo cameras through the separate camera permissions
Discovery, enrollment and control each need your permission and a control agent grant
Finding a device does not mean Bridgit can control it

title: Add a control agent in a minute
description: Bridgit makes a setup prompt with the control agent's own key, the address and the rules. Paste it into any AI control agent and it can use the phone straight away.
example: You add Claude: name it, copy the prompt, paste it into Claude. The screen turns to "Claude connected" as soon as it calls.

title: One key per control agent
description: Every control agent has its own key. Rotate it or remove the control agent in one tap; the old key stops at once and the control agent is told why.
example: You pasted Grok's prompt into the wrong chat. Rotate Grok's key; the leaked one is dead in a second.

title: Take a photo
description: A control agent can take a photo with the front or back camera. Android's green dot and a Bridgit notification show every time.
example: From your laptop: "Is the stove off?" Your control agent takes a photo of the kitchen and tells you.
options: Back or front camera
Zoom: 0.5× (ultra-wide) up to the phone's maximum (telephoto)
Flash on or off
Size: sized for AI (1568 px), thumbnail (512 px), large (2560 px) or original
Or an exact width or long edge, and JPEG quality
Full resolution, up to the 50 MP sensor
As JSON with the picture inside, or as plain JPEG bytes
Never saved to your gallery

title: Record a short clip
description: A control agent can record 1 to 120 seconds of audio and get it back as a file.
example: "Listen to the next 30 seconds of the meeting and give me the action items."
options: Length: 1 to 120 whole seconds
Comes back as an M4A (AAC) audio file, 44.1 kHz mono
Not kept on the phone

title: Your latest screenshot or photo
description: One call returns the newest screenshot or camera photo, sized for an AI to read. It can also wait for the next one you take.
example: You screenshot an error on your phone; your control agent already has it and explains the fix.
options: Which: any image, the newest screenshot, or the newest camera photo
Wait up to 55 seconds for the next one you take
Size: sized for AI (default), thumbnail, large or original
As JSON or as plain JPEG bytes, with when it was taken and the album

title: Find photos in your gallery
description: Control agents can list recent images and fetch one at the size they need. Bridgit never edits or deletes anything.
example: "Find the receipt photo from this morning and add it to my expenses."
options: List the newest 1 to 100 images (no pictures, just details)
Fetch one image at any of the sizes
Works with full access or only the photos you picked

title: Everything is logged
description: Every request, switch change and control agent note is in Activity on the phone. Control agents can read and follow the log too, so they know what they did.
example: Codex checks yesterday's log to see why a photo failed; you scroll Activity to see who did what.
options: Filter by control agent, type, endpoint, result, level, time or text
Follow it live
Stats per control agent and endpoint
Export as JSONL or CSV
"All entries" or "only their own" for control agents

title: Control agent notes
description: Control agents can write short notes into the log.
example: Your fridge-check control agent writes "milk low" so you see it in Activity.

title: The API explains itself
description: Control agents read a live guide and an OpenAPI file that list what's switched on, every call and every error.
example: A brand-new control agent reads the guide and learns everything without a manual.

title: Control agents learn what's new
description: Every reply says which API revision Bridgit speaks. After an update, control agents are told there's something new until they read the list of changes, so they pick up new features by themselves.
example: Bridgit gains camera zoom; the next time Grok calls, it reads what's new and starts using zoom.

title: Report a bug or ask for a feature
description: From any screen: the last screen is attached, plus screenshots and the recent log. Control agents in Bridgit Fixer Mode read reports and mark them fixed; you confirm or say it's still broken.
example: The app misbehaves; you report it in 10 seconds. Claude picks it up, fixes it and marks it fixed.
options: Last screen, up to 5 screenshots and the recent log attached
Turn off "Auto-fix" to keep it for a person
Statuses: new, seen, in progress, fixed, won't fix, duplicate
You confirm a fix or say it's still broken

title: Check for updates
description: Bridgit finds a new version, checks it really is Bridgit, and lets Android install it after you confirm.
example: A fix ships; your phone offers the update the next time you open Bridgit.

title: You stay in control
description: Every feature starts off and has its own switch. Pause listening in one tap. Access shows each Android permission with one button to the right page.
example: Going into a meeting: turn off Camera and Microphone from Home in two taps.

title: Only over Tailscale
description: Bridgit answers only on your private Tailscale network, never the open internet.
example: Your control agents on your Mac and your server can reach the phone; nobody else can.

title: Questions and notices to you
description: Control agents send you a notice, or a question with buttons, choices or a text reply, and get your answer within a second of your tap. They can also read it aloud.
example: "Pay this invoice? $11.99" [Pay] [Not now]. You tap Pay on the notification; the control agent pays.
options: A notice (one-way) or a question
Buttons (up to 6), a text reply, a choice list, or a link
An image with the message
Normal or urgent; read aloud if you allow it
Expires after 1 minute to 7 days
The control agent waits for your answer or gets a callback

title: Rich HTML cards
description: Instead of plain buttons, a control agent can send a small HTML page (charts, forms, choices) that runs safely on the phone with no internet access.
example: Your travel control agent shows three flights as cards with prices and a map; you tap one to book.
options: A small HTML page with its own layout, charts and forms
Runs on the phone with no internet access
Sends one answer back to the control agent (up to 16 KB of data)
Images inside the card only (data: images), up to 256 KB of HTML
Bridgit's own header shows which control agent sent it; you can always dismiss it

title: Live text panel
description: A control agent streams text into the lower half of the screen and it scrolls as it arrives, like the transcript of an AI session. Pause the scrolling or close it any time.
example: Claude Code is fixing a bug on your laptop; you watch what it's doing on the phone while you make coffee.
options: Lower half of the screen, scrolls as text arrives
Pause scrolling to read, then resume
The control agent marks it finished; you close it whenever you like
Keeps the last 200 KB of text

title: Use Bridgit over MCP
description: Control agents that speak MCP (Claude Code, Codex and others) add Bridgit as a tool server with their own key, and every feature appears as a tool.
example: Add Bridgit to Claude Code once; from then on "take a photo of my desk" just works.
options: Same key, same switches, same log as the normal API

title: Inbox
description: One place for every question, notice, file and share between you and your control agents.
example: See what Grok asked you this morning and what you answered.

title: Send a screenshot
description: A control agent sees what's on your screen right now, with no prompt each time; a notification shows every capture.
example: "What does this error on my phone mean?" The control agent takes a screenshot and reads it.

Turn on Bridgit's screenshot service once (Hardware access), then Screenshots in Feature enablement

title: Events and callbacks
description: Control agents get told the moment something happens: a question answered, a new screenshot, a switch changed.
example: Your control agent waits for your answer without asking again and again.

title: Open a link or app

title: Quick Settings tile
description: Pause or resume Bridgit from the notification shade.
example: Pull down, tap Bridgit, and control agents can't reach the phone until you tap again.

title: Phone status and context
description: Battery (level, charging, health, temperature, battery saver), network, ringer, Do Not Disturb and screen/lock status. Control agents hear when the battery runs low or starts charging. An unlocked interactive screen is reported as in use.

title: Location details
description: Where the phone is, on request only: latitude and longitude (x, y), altitude (z), accuracy, speed and heading, and how old the fix is. Address lookup if you turn it on. No tracking unless you choose it.
example: "How long until I'm home?" The control agent checks where you are and the traffic.

title: Weather
description: The forecast where the phone is, or anywhere the control agent names: now, the next hours and today's low and high, from MET Norway. Your position is rounded to about 1 km first. Control agents can check it on a schedule.
example: Every morning at 7 your control agent checks the weather and tells you to take an umbrella.

Turn off now
Ask whether it's on

title: App settings
description: Every Bridgit setting and the phone's sound and display settings in one place. Any control agent can read them; control agents with Agent Super Powers can change them once you allow it. Control agents can never stop the listener, change their own permissions or turn this switch back on.
example: "Switch Bridgit to dark mode, keep the log for 90 days and turn the media volume down to 30%."
